key_insight: FAERS data suggest certain medications are associated with hidradenitis suppurativa signals, including paradoxical reactions to some HS treatments and possible drug-induced cases.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help clinicians recognize and monitor for HS onset or flares after starting implicated drugs, especially biologics and select antineoplastics.
method: Reviewed FAERS reports from 2003–2023 for hidradenitis suppurativa.
Separated reports into drug-worsened (HS listed as an indication) vs drug-induced (HS not listed).
Used reporting odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals and time-to-onset analysis.
evidence_signal: The study identified 5,529 HS reports overall, including 1,804 drug-induced and 3,725 drug-worsened cases, with significant reporting signals for adalimumab, infliximab, secukinumab, isotretinoin, cytarabine, and omacetaxine.
watch_item: FAERS signals are based on spontaneous reports and cannot prove causation; indication bias and underreporting may affect interpretation.
paper_title: Patient-Level Risk Characterization of Drug-Associated Hidradenitis Suppurativa Using Machine Learning
